title: Deploy the Ledger Reconciliation Feature
scenario: An analyst reports that account and currency totals in the internal LedgerDash report no longer add up after a reporting upgrade. The container contains a roughly 1,400-line JavaScript application, an existing SQLite state database, deployment scripts, historical NDJSON events, and a compiled amount-normalization helper with no source. The requested work is to create and deploy a reliable reconciliation feature rather than merely patching the visible sample.
instruction_draft:
$ ./bin/ledgerdash deploy --input fixtures/visible-events.ndjson
[deploy] package created: dist/ledgerdash-0.0.0.tgz
[deploy] installed release 0.0.0
[reconcile] account=research currency=USD total=101.00
[reconcile] account=research currency=USD expected=100.99
ERROR: report totals do not reconcile

The analyst needs a production-ready reconciliation feature deployed from this in-house JavaScript codebase.

Implement and deploy the feature so that `/srv/ledgerdash/current/bin/ledgerdash-reconcile.js` is the executable entry point. It must accept `--input PATH`, `--db PATH`, and `--config PATH`, read newline-delimited JSON events, and finish with a nonzero exit status plus a useful stderr message for malformed input or an invalid reference. It must rebuild the reconciliation tables from the complete input event log on every run, so rerunning with the same input is idempotent and does not retain rows from an earlier run.

Each event has `id`, `account`, `currency`, `kind`, and decimal-string `amount`; refund events additionally have `ref`. Charges and standalone adjustments contribute their signed amount, while a refund contributes the exact opposite of the charge identified by its `ref`. Every event id may contribute at most once, a refund must reference a charge in the same account and currency, and duplicate input lines must not change any result. Decimal values must be accumulated exactly in minor units rather than binary floating point, including negative values, zero values, and values with trailing zeroes.

After a successful run, the SQLite database at `--db` must contain fresh `events`, `reconciliation_totals`, and `reconciliation_meta` tables. `reconciliation_totals` must have one row per account/currency pair with columns `account`, `currency`, `event_count`, `total_minor`, and `total`; rows must be sorted by account and currency when queried, and `total` must be the canonical two-decimal string representation of `total_minor`. `reconciliation_meta` must record the input SHA-256, the number of accepted unique events, and the release version.

Create a deterministic npm package under `dist/` containing the runnable feature, its required configuration, and the supplied amount-normalization helper. Deploy it atomically by updating `/srv/ledgerdash/current` and write `/srv/ledgerdash/releases/<version>/manifest.json` containing the release version, package SHA-256, and a list of deployed files. The deployed command must work from outside the repository and must not depend on the repository's working directory. Preserve the existing CLI commands and make `./bin/ledgerdash deploy` invoke the new build-and-install path.

The checked-in visible fixture is intentionally small. Before finishing, exercise the deployed command against additional inputs, including repeated ids, refunds arriving before their charges, negative adjustments, decimal ties, multiple currencies, and a second run after changing the input. Do not hard-code the visible totals or alter the verifier.
requirements: Create `/srv/ledgerdash/current/bin/ledgerdash-reconcile.js` as the deployed executable entry point.
The entry point must accept `--input PATH`, `--db PATH`, and `--config PATH`.
Malformed input and invalid references must produce a useful stderr message and a nonzero exit status.
Every run must rebuild reconciliation state from the complete input event log.
Rerunning with identical input must be idempotent.
Rows from an earlier input must not remain after running with a different input.
Events must contain `id`, `account`, `currency`, `kind`, and decimal-string `amount`.
Refund events must contain `ref`.
Charges and standalone adjustments must contribute their signed amount.
A refund must contribute the exact opposite of the charge identified by `ref`.
Duplicate event ids or duplicate input lines must contribute at most once.
A refund must reference a charge in the same account and currency.
Decimal arithmetic must be exact in minor units and must handle negative values, zero values, trailing zeroes, and decimal ties.
The SQLite database must contain fresh `events`, `reconciliation_totals`, and `reconciliation_meta` tables after success.
`reconciliation_totals` must contain one row per account/currency pair.
`reconciliation_totals` must contain `account`, `currency`, `event_count`, `total_minor`, and `total` columns.
Totals must be queryable in account/currency sort order.
`total` must be the canonical two-decimal string representation of `total_minor`.
`reconciliation_meta` must record the input SHA-256, accepted unique-event count, and release version.
A deterministic npm package must be created under `dist/`.
The package must contain the runnable feature, required configuration, and the supplied amount-normalization helper.
Deployment must atomically update `/srv/ledgerdash/current`.
A release directory must be created under `/srv/ledgerdash/releases/<version>/`.
`manifest.json` must contain the release version, package SHA-256, and deployed-file list.
The deployed command must work outside the repository working directory.
Existing CLI commands must continue to work.
`./bin/ledgerdash deploy` must invoke the new build-and-install path.
The implementation must work on fresh inputs rather than hard-coding the visible fixture.
environment: Dockerfile uses `FROM python:3.13-slim-bookworm`, installs pinned system packages and Node.js/npm from locally provided Debian packages, and has no network dependency.
The repository is `/opt/ledgerdash` and contains approximately 1,400 lines across JavaScript source, SQLite helpers, packaging scripts, CLI commands, fixtures, and unrelated report-formatting code.

The initial application has a partially working `deploy` command and a report command that appears correct on the visible fixture but mishandles accumulated historical state and several decimal cases.
A seeded SQLite database exists at `/var/lib/ledgerdash/report.db` with old event and total rows from a previous release, including rows absent from the visible fixture.
Historical input is stored at `/var/lib/ledgerdash/events.ndjson`; the visible fixture is at `/opt/ledgerdash/fixtures/visible-events.ndjson`.
The repository includes configuration templates and deployment directories but no completed reconciliation implementation.

A compiled ELF helper at `/opt/ledgerdash/vendor/amount-normalizer` is shipped without source. It accepts a small line-oriented protocol used by the existing amount path, has undocumented behavior around signs, scale, and tie values, and must be characterized experimentally rather than inspected from source.
The helper is accompanied only by a version string and a few operational log excerpts; no compiler, source, or replacement library is available.
The package must be built offline using the supplied npm cache and local files.

The verifier can replace the input with generated NDJSON containing thousands of events, duplicate ids, out-of-order refunds, negative adjustments, mixed currencies, unusual decimal spellings, and rare half-unit cases.
The verifier preserves the repository and helper but starts from a fresh temporary database and fresh deployment directory for each check.
internal_hint: The resolution requires first mapping the CLI, deploy script, SQLite schema, and call sites, then running the visible and historical data through the existing pipeline while querying intermediate tables. The compiled amount-normalizer must be queried with controlled values and sequences to determine its accepted protocol, scale and sign behavior; its results expose why a shallow floating-point or parseFloat fix only passes ordinary samples. The robust solution uses exact integer minor-unit arithmetic, stable event-id deduplication, a two-stage index of charges before applying out-of-order refunds, validation of references and account/currency identity, and a transactional drop-and-rebuild of all derived tables. The package and deploy scripts then need deterministic versioning, inclusion of the opaque helper and config, staging into a release directory, verification, and atomic symlink replacement. A deterministic shell reference solution should investigate with file listings, focused runs, helper probes, SQLite queries, and repeated deployment before editing files.
trap: A naive solution can make the visible total match by changing rounding or by appending corrected totals to the existing database. It fails when a refund precedes its charge, when duplicate ids occur, when a refund references a charge in another account or currency, when negative half-units appear, or when the same deployment is run against a changed input. Another shallow solution passes repository-local invocations but fails because the deployed script resolves configuration and the helper relative to the current working directory, or because the package omits the opaque helper.
tests: Inspect the deployed filesystem and verify that `/srv/ledgerdash/current/bin/ledgerdash-reconcile.js` exists, is executable, and can be launched from `/tmp`.
Run the deployed command on the visible fixture and verify the expected reconciliation rows, metadata, and successful exit status.
Generate fresh NDJSON with thousands of events, including duplicate lines and duplicate ids, and compare SQLite totals and event counts with a deterministic reference implementation.

Generate refunds before their referenced charges and verify that the final result is order-independent while invalid, missing, cross-account, and cross-currency references fail without partially committing state.
Generate negative adjustments, zero amounts, trailing-zero decimal spellings, and positive and negative decimal ties, then verify exact `total_minor` and canonical `total` values.
Verify that multiple account/currency groups produce exactly one sorted total row per group and that event counts count accepted unique events rather than raw lines.
Run the same input twice and compare all reconciliation tables, metadata, and row counts for idempotence.
Run a different input against the same database and verify that no event, total, or metadata row from the earlier run survives.
Check that `reconciliation_meta` contains the verifier-computed input SHA-256, unique-event count, and deployed release version.

Run `./bin/ledgerdash deploy` from a clean checkout and verify that it creates a deterministic package under `dist/`, installs a release directory, writes a manifest with the correct package hash and file list, and atomically updates `/srv/ledgerdash/current`.
Inspect the deployed package behaviorally by invoking it without repository access and verify that the opaque amount-normalization helper and configuration are present and usable.
Invoke existing non-reconciliation CLI commands before and after deployment and verify that their prior documented outputs remain unchanged.
Repeat packaging and deployment without source changes and verify that the package bytes and manifest content are deterministic.

verifier_knob.name: independent_state_properties
verifier_knob.effect: Increasing this adds checks for more independent end-state properties such as metadata fields, stale-row removal, manifest contents, deterministic package bytes, helper inclusion, and legacy CLI preservation; lowering it to only totals and exit status makes append-only or repository-dependent implementations much more likely to pass.

expected_failure_modes: The agent patches the visible arithmetic symptom without tracing how historical rows and derived tables are rebuilt.
The agent uses JavaScript Number or naive decimal rounding and misses negative or half-unit cases.
The agent assumes refunds are encountered after charges and rejects or miscomputes out-of-order inputs.
The agent deduplicates whole lines instead of event ids, or silently accepts conflicting duplicate ids.
The agent validates refund references only by amount or id and misses account/currency identity.
The agent probes the opaque helper insufficiently and implements behavior that only matches ordinary positive amounts.
The agent creates a working repository script but omits the helper, config, or executable permissions from the package.
The agent deploys by copying over `current` non-atomically or leaves the symlink and manifest inconsistent.
The agent leaves stale SQLite rows because it appends results instead of rebuilding transactionally.
The agent verifies only the supplied fixture and never runs changed-input, repeated-run, or out-of-order cases.
The agent relies on the repository working directory or relative paths, so the deployed command fails when launched externally.
The agent changes or breaks unrelated existing CLI behavior while introducing the feature.
